result.title: MA-Bench: Measuring Operational Planning in Language Models
result.summary: How well can a language model turn a large, incomplete and partly contradictory body of documents into a plan when no single correct answer exists? We introduce Mission Analysis (MA)-Bench, built on mission analysis, the first step of military operational planning, in which a staff reads the full situation and states the problem before anyone proposes a solution. Its 10 expert-built scenarios pair synthetic packets of ten to twelve documents with 1,257 expert-written pass/fail requirements, each containing information on their source, question type, and importance level. A reasoning-model judge grades each brief against the requirements without seeing the documents; it grades like a fifth credentialed planner, leaving a four-planner panel's agreement unchanged (Fleiss $κ$ 0.42 to 0.41), and a judge from a second provider reproduces the model ranking (Spearman 0.94). Across twenty frontier and open-weights models the best gets 62% of the rubric items right. Models are strongest on facts stated in the documents (58%) and weakest on judgments that must be inferred (33%), and six failures in ten are omissions rather than errors. MA-Bench grades the determinations, not the prose. We release the packets, rubrics, prompts, scorer and every graded brief with item-level verdicts.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 MA-Bench：用 10 个专家构建的军事「任务分析」场景（每场景 10–12 份合成文档加 1,257 条人工通过的 rubric），考察语言模型在信息不全且部分矛盾时能否先界定问题再成文，并以推理模型作为第五位评分者；结果显示最强模型仅答对 62%，需推断的判断最弱（33%），六成失败是遗漏而非错误。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本规划评测，与视觉 latent 状态无直接机制联系；但其 rubric 条目级评分、评分者一致性验证（Fleiss κ、跨模型 Spearman 复现）以及「遗漏多于错误」的失败分类，可能为 LVR 的推理过程评价、证据筛选诊断与停止/覆盖率度量提供参照。
